newsitem.title: UK: National Grid accepts price control change. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: National Grid accepts price control change. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]

text.p: Electricity transmission company National Grid Plc said it has accepted in principle electricity industry regulator OFFER's proposals for changes to the transmission price control.
The company said it considered its decision to be in the best interests of shareholders and employees to avoid further uncertainty, delay and diversion of management time.

OFFER put foward its proposals in October. They include a one-off reduction in the first year of the new controls from April 1, 1997 of 20 percent, followed by a cap on price increases of RPI -4, four points below inflation, for the following three years to 2001.

National Grid made no comment on OFFER's revised proposals but had called its original proposals of a 20 to 26 pct price cut range, "contrived, illogical and inconsistent". OFFER chief Stephen Littlechild said they were tough but realistic.
(Corrects to make clear that National Grid made no comment on OFFER's revised proposals, the comments ascribed to it having been made in connection with OFFER's original proposals).
"These proposals will create a challenging environment for the regulated transmission business," said National Grid chief executive David Jones in a statement on Friday.
"Although we will be introducing further measures to improve efficiency...the proposed reductions in revenue will have a material impact on transmission business profitability."
Jones added that he was confident of maintaining a "progressive" dividend policy.
